title: Good blues piano players and their repertoire
summary: Amacker names the old blues pianists (Sam Henry, Kitchen, Ollie Sullivan, Birmingham) and the pieces and original blues like Jelly Roll Blues they played.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you something else. Who were some of the good blues piano players around town when you were young?

Sam Henry, a friend called Sam Henry, old timer. Another friend called Kitchen, he was his name. Sam Henry, Kitchen. And another one called Ollie Sullivan. And another one called Ollie Sullivan. In that day they were good blue players. In that day Kitchen, Sam Henry, Ollie Sullivan. And as you mentioned Birmingham, you knew him, that's his name, blues. Birmingham was another one. And that's Kitchen, Sam Henry, Birmingham, Ollie Sullivan. Did they play anything else about blues? Well, they played a lot of old house pieces in that day, you know. Mostly a lot of playing blues. First one blues was another.
What would be some of the pieces?

Some of the pieces in that day would be some of the old pieces such as a very big beautiful doll, you know. You know that old number of the very big beautiful doll. You know that old piece? That'd be there to feature that. Another number to be there is about there. Another number they used to be crazy about, that they'd feature a lot is Rufus Rastus, Johnson Brown, and Peter Raff.
Did they have any old original blues that they made up themselves?

Yeah. Such as, now original blues, one of the original blues was the master blues, was the Jell-O-Roll blues. It wasn't the master blues in that day, because the fellas played it in that day, from one to another. But in this day the men don't see and be understand how to play that Jell-O-Roll blues, you know. But they played it in that day, you see, from one to another. They were all cracker-jacks along that line in that day, you know. That line in that day. They were very good in that day. But of course now the men can't play the moon out like that.
